statusDefinitions.implemented: Code and an executable test or gate exist; final environment-specific evidence may still be pending.
statusDefinitions.verified: The checked-in automated evidence path exercises the behavior without a skipped or fabricated result.
statusDefinitions.externally_blocked: The executable gate exists but requires credentials, infrastructure, or independent authority unavailable to this repository.

requirements.behavior: A clean npm install resolves the declared compiler, React, schema, and MCP runtime without undeclared global modules.
One canonical acceptance command discovers nested tests and fails on missing, failed, timed-out, or empty required gates.
Tenant and project authorization is applied independently to HTTP reads, writes, jobs, artifacts, tokens, and provider records.
Private conversation ownership is enforced in addition to membership and transcripts are encrypted at rest.
Tool calls remain limited to reviewed capabilities with exact confirmation, leases, replay fencing, and outcome-uncertain handling.
Provider and runner output is size-bounded, schema-validated, budgeted, cancellable, and never silently replaced by a fixture.
limitations: Live provider authentication is tracked separately in V23-OPS-03.

requirements.behavior: Project-native React source is typechecked and bundled by exact declared dependencies with integrity-bound output.
Every supplied source kit runs actual Chromium tasks across ready, loading, empty, error, responsive, theme, and RTL cases.
limitations: Canonical acceptance regenerates evidence for all nine supplied kits.

requirements.behavior: Approval, signature, current project-version checks, and revocation are distinct mandatory component lifecycle gates.
Production certification refuses local subprocess mode and provides a network-disabled least-privilege container invocation.
limitations: A deployment registry must still scan the exact promoted digest.

requirements.behavior: Normal Chromium navigation completes Studio login, cookie and CSRF handling, component preview, host chat, confirmation, write, reload, and mobile layout.
limitations: Uses an explicitly labelled controlled model fixture; live models are tracked separately.

requirements.behavior: Conversation cancellation, retry, attachments, feedback, artifact revision, pinning, and purge have durable scoped service behavior.
Published artifact access rechecks current component signature, project version, recipient authorization, and revocation.
Coding agents receive read-only project-scoped MCP search, model, component, source, and versioned skill resources.
MCP uses the current pinned protocol, exposes published components only, and observes token revocation on the next request.
Project models retain source provenance, capability confidence, design genome, API contracts, and stable version identities.
Opt-in semantic telemetry records bounded shapes and mines workflow opportunities without capturing payload values.
Project and policy version changes invalidate incompatible artifacts while reusable published artifacts avoid another design call.
The supported deployment is documented and enforced as single-host SQLite WAL with graceful API and worker shutdown.
limitations: No multi-host high-availability claim is made.

requirements.behavior: Migration checksums, backup restoration, signing-key rotation and compromised-key revocation have executable drills.
Scoped live API and CLI provider accounts complete bounded generation jobs without fixture substitution.
limitations: Authenticated Claude Opus 4.8/high and Codex CLI adapter calls passed locally. No scoped API key was supplied, so the required API half remains blocked and no fallback was used.

requirements.behavior: The production Linux certifier and service images install locked runtimes, build, execute, and run actual network-disabled browser certification at recorded image IDs.
limitations: Local immutable image IDs are evidence for this build only; the deployment registry must scan and attest the promoted digests.

requirements.behavior: An independent security reviewer completes penetration, dependency, and multi-tenant threat-model review against the final commit.
limitations: Independent reviewer identity and signed report are external authority and cannot be self-attested by the implementation agent.

requirements.behavior: README, architecture, integration, MCP, provider, security, operations, testing, and release documents describe only current implemented commands and limits.
limitations: Documentation validation checks paths and commands; human editorial review remains advisable.
